_comment: COUPLING tier-2. 'aitken' is the `couple` tool's DEFAULT accelerator, and this fixture is what stands behind the corrected sentence attached to the knowledge's own divergence example: at rho = 4, theta = 0.5 a CONSTANT theta diverges (measured 4.1e+13 relative at 300 iterations) while the DEFAULT 'does NOT diverge on this case, and it does not solve it either: it lands on the closed-form interface value to 1.2e-05 relative and its residual is still 1.4e-04 against tol = 1e-4 after 300 iterations'. ||| WHAT CHANGED AND WHY. It used to test the previous sentence, 'the default aitken survives this particular case', read as converged=True, and it was red. That sentence came from a 40-cell sweep run on the PER-PARTICIPANT Aitken theta that feature/coupling-robustness replaced with one global theta, on an analytic stand-in for the participants, at tol=1e-8 over 400 iterations, with a harness that was never committed. Re-measured on the shipped driver with scripts/sweep_accelerators.py, the default here does not diverge and does not converge: it sits on the right answer with a residual that will not come down, because its own adaptation drives theta onto the 0.05 clamp (60 of 299 adaptations) and the residual can then only fall like (1-theta) per iteration, measured at 0.968. The knowledge now says that and this fixture now tests it. ||| THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT. `converged` and 'found the answer' give OPPOSITE verdicts on the same run here, and an agent that reads converged=False as 'the physics is wrong' goes and changes the physics. So BOTH halves are asserted: that the interface state really is the analytic one — temperature and flux from both sides with the two outward normals' opposite signs, plus the conservation balance — and that the residual really did not reach tol. Either half alone would pass a broken driver: the first accepts a run that never settles, the second accepts one that settled on the wrong fixed point. ||| BUDGET. max_iter moved from 200 to 300 with the claim, because the sweep behind the claim gave every cell of its 70-setting grid the same max_iter=300. At 200 the Aitken arm has landed on the interface VALUE (3.1e-04) but its interface flux is still 0.30 W/m^2 from the closed form against the 0.2 tolerance used here, so the physics half could not be checked and 'landed on the answer' would have rested on the temperature alone. Both arms share the identical budget and tol, which is the property that matters — without it the comparison is between an accelerator and a budget.

_mutation.note: Point the second arm at the constant accelerator too, so the surviving arm becomes the diverging one. Both arms then run the case the knowledge says diverges: aitken_diverged prints True, the interface state ends orders of magnitude from the closed form so aitken_landed_on_the_closed_form prints False, the physics checks fire, and the vacuity guard the_two_arms_ran_different_accelerators prints False as well. A fixture that merely ran the default and checked it did not crash would survive this; one that races the default against the constant it is supposed to outlast cannot.
